A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Synthetic Bootstrapped Pretraining with the same authors, method, and research objective. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original pretraining experiments, benchmark results, synthetic-data evaluations, mixture ablations, and additional model-scaling experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds 6B-model SBP experiments, synthetic-data evaluations, and a random-pair control in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The nearest-neighbor pairing, conditional synthesizer-tuning objective, sampling procedure, and joint pretraining method remain unchanged. The 6B architecture already appeared in v1 Appendix C.2; applying SBP at that size extends experimentation without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same curated DCLM source and nine evaluation benchmarks. The added model-size and random-pair experiments reuse existing coverage; MMLU's revised scoring changes the evaluation protocol rather than introducing another dataset or domain.

E2.justification: V3 Appendix A.3 and Table 4 add a synthesizer trained on random document pairs as a comparator for generated-document relevance, alongside random document-pair controls. The main repetition and oracle comparators and Appendix C's existing 6B baseline are retained.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 replaces five-shot MMLU accuracy with perplexity over demonstrations, questions, and correct answers, also removing MMLU from QA averages. V3 adds a 6B, 1T-token SBP setting with 50B unique source tokens and a 0/125B/250B synthetic-token sweep, plus an embedding-similarity protocol for the random-pair control.

E4.justification: V3 adds a mechanism-focused ablation testing whether semantic rather than random pairing preserves seed-output relevance (Appendix A.3). It also adds a 6B synthetic-mixture sensitivity study (Figure 8) and extends synthetic-data quality diagnostics to that model (Table 2), substantially broadening the analysis beyond v1's 3B studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional experiments retain point-estimate reporting; the new similarity means do not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New 6B results include mean QA gains over repetition of 1.32 percentage points for SBP versus 2.26 for the oracle (Table 1), and 6.5% non-factual synthetic documents (Table 2). Table 4 adds generated-document similarities of 0.66 for SBP versus 0.32 for random-pair training. MMLU accuracy results are replaced by perplexities throughout, including Appendix C, with recalculated QA averages. Figure 7 also changes the 250B-mixture OpenWebText2 perplexity from approximately 4.88 to 4.49.

T1.justification: The optimization objectives, hierarchical latent-concept model, conditional-independence assumption, and Bayesian derivation in Sections 2 and 5 remain substantively unchanged. There are no added proofs or formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion extend the main SBP validation claim from 3B to both 3B and 6B models. The abstract now specifies recovery of up to 60% of the oracle improvement rather than an unspecified significant fraction. The proposed framework and Bayesian contribution remain the same.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the larger-model results as favorable scaling and attributes the higher selected synthetic-data proportion to greater model capacity. It extends the factuality explanation to model size, interprets the random-pair control as evidence of learned semantic relevance, and explains the MMLU metric substitution. Existing limitations largely remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 discloses resource costs for the added 6B setting: 265K v5p-TPU hours for pretraining and 8.4K B200 hours for synthesis. Appendix A.3 identifies the embedding model and source dataset used for its new diagnostic. Existing implementation details and resource-access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work discussion are unchanged after matching references across pagination and hyphenation. Positioning relative to teacher-based synthesis, retrieval-augmented models, and conventional pretraining remains the same.

P1.justification: V3 adds Appendix A.3, expands the MMLU evaluation explanation, and locally revises the abstract, experimental narrative, discussion, and conclusion for the 6B results. The overall section organization and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 expand for the 6B setting; Figures 6–7 reorganize benchmark panels and replace MMLU accuracy axes with perplexity. V3 adds the similarity table and a 6B mixture figure, with later appendix displays renumbered and shifted. The established layout and visual style remain largely intact.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens v1's empirical support by evaluating SBP itself at 6B, adding mixture analysis, and introducing a random-pair relevance control. These provide useful evidence about scalability and pairing behavior. The gains are bounded: the control measures relevance without downstream pretraining results, and replacing MMLU accuracy with perplexity trades direct task-performance evidence for a smoother proxy. Overall, the revision offers a limited but supported quality improvement.
